newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Asset swaps boost Sasol stocks - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Asset swaps boost Sasol stocks - dealers.

text.p: Asset swaps worth almost 50 million rand boosted trade in South African chemicals to oils group Sasol Ltd on Wednesday, hoisting the share price more than two percent higher, dealers said.
"There were three corporate finance deals in Sasol. Asset swaps? Yes, that's the right word for it," a dealer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said.
Traders said broking firm Deutsche Morgan Grenfell had done one deal in 300,000 shares, with BOE Natwest responsible for two further transactions in a total of 520,000 shares.
Volume in Sasol, which at 1330 GMT was at 1.42 million shares worth over 78 million rand, was also further propped up by two large bookover trades, dealers said.
Sasol was last trading 125 cents higher or up 2.3 percent, at 55.25 rand.
Asset swaps, whereby South African institutions swap holdings with overseas counterparts, have become almost a daily occurence on the Johannesburg bourse.
Local institutions, under foreign exchange control regulations, can use this mechanism to invest a portion of their assets offshore.
